title: Arrays and Lists
summary: Fixed-size arrays and growable List<T> - creating, indexing, ranges and Index from the end, iterating, adding, inserting and removing, searching, sorting with comparisons, copying versus sharing, collection expressions, and two-dimensional and jagged arrays.

cards.q: Why remove items from a list inside a loop by going backwards?
cards.a:
Removing shifts later items down; going backwards, the indexes still to visit do not move

Removing at i moves every later item down one place. Counting forwards with a for loop then silently skips an item; it does not throw (foreach is the loop that throws when the list changes).

cards.q: After var b = a; b.Add(1); does a contain the 1?
cards.a:
Yes: a and b refer to the same list

A List is a reference type, so `b = a` copies the reference, not the items. To copy the list, write `new List<int>(a)`.

-1

IndexOf returns -1 when the value is not in the list.
